full_text_en:
Tang Min Defamation Case

Private Prosecutor: Zhu Xiuqin, female, 43 years old, family planning officer of Panxi Township, Fuding County, Fujian Province.

Private Prosecutor: Zhu Liangfa, male, 50 years old, deputy director of the Construction Committee of Fuding County, Fujian Province, elder brother of Zhu Xiuqin.

Private Prosecutor: Shen Zhenzhu, female, 47 years old, employee of the Fisheries and Fishing Supplies Station of Fuding County, Fujian Province, wife of Zhu Liangfa.

Defendant: Tang Min, female, 34 years old, formerly a writer at the Xiamen Federation of Literary and Art Circles, Fujian Province. Was arrested on December 26, 1989.

Private Prosecutors Zhu Xiuqin, Zhu Liangfa, and Shen Zhenzhu filed a lawsuit with the Siming District People's Court of Xiamen, Fujian Province, accusing Defendant Tang Min of using her novel to defame the deceased Wang Lianzhong and the private prosecutors, requesting that criminal liability be pursued, and demanding compensation for the economic losses suffered by the private prosecutors as a result of Tang Min's defamation. The Siming District People's Court formed a collegial panel according to law. After a public trial, the court found the following facts:

The medium-length documentary novel "The Evil Atmosphere of Mount Taimu" written by Defendant Tang Min was published in the February 1986 issue (No. 2) of the literary monthly "Youth" in Nanjing. The novel used the real name, real address, and the actual kinship titles between Wang Lianzhong (who died in a work-related accident in 1979), the husband of Private Prosecutor Zhu Xiuqin, and the three private prosecutors. Employing rumors circulating in society and fabricated facts, it described Wang Lianzhong's actions during his tenure as militia battalion commander: that he tyrannized the village, arbitrarily arrested and imprisoned people, hung and beat villagers, robbed people of their money, raided others' wedding banquets, forced the groom to death, and drove the bride insane; that Wang Lianzhong was able to do so because he relied on the power of his wife's brother, Private Prosecutor Zhu Liangfa, who served as deputy secretary of the Commune Party Committee; that Zhu Liangfa, having lost his principles, persuaded the production brigade to accept Wang Lianzhong into the Party; that after Wang Lianzhong's death he turned into a calf, and Zhu Xiuqin developed "affection" for the calf, forgetting all human shame; and that Shen Zhenzhu had committed adultery with others. After the novel was published, the reputation of the three private prosecutors was seriously damaged. Zhu Xiuqin, subjected to public criticism, almost committed suicide, and her son ran away from home. Zhu Liangfa's work was severely affected. Shen Zhenzhu felt too ashamed to face others. The three private prosecutors also suffered certain economic losses due to the lawsuit.

The Siming District People's Court held that: Defendant Tang Min, who had lived in the locality of the private prosecutors for many years, was familiar with the deceased Wang Lianzhong and well aware of the kinship relations between the three private prosecutors and Wang Lianzhong, yet she intentionally fabricated false facts to defame them, using vile means with serious circumstances. Her conduct constituted the crime of defamation as provided in Article 145 of the Criminal Law of the PRC. The request of the three private prosecutors for compensation of the economic losses caused by Tang Min's defamation conformed to the provisions of Article 31 of the Criminal Law and should be affirmed. Given that this case was a private prosecution case, the court first conducted mediation in accordance with Article 127 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC. However, because Tang Min refused to admit her guilt, mediation was ineffective. Accordingly, on January 10, 1990, the Siming District People's Court rendered the following judgment: 1. Defendant Tang Min is guilty of defamation and is sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year. 2. Defendant Tang Min shall compensate the private prosecutors Zhu Xiuqin, Zhu Liangfa, and Shen Zhenzhu for economic losses in the amount of 2,000 yuan.

Defendant Tang Min refused to accept the first-instance judgment and appealed to the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court.

The Xiamen Intermediate People's Court on appeal held that: Appellant Tang Min, by using rumors and fabricated facts in her own novel, publicly insulted and defamed others, causing serious damage to the reputations of the deceased Wang Lianzhong and the three private prosecutors. This was an intentional crime. The original judgment had accurate characterization, appropriate sentencing, legal procedure, and reasonable compensation, and should be affirmed. Tang Min's grounds for appeal were not sustainable. On March 3, 1990, pursuant to item (1) of Article 136 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the court ruled: the appeal of Appellant Tang Min was rejected and the original judgment was affirmed.
